definition: Data provenance records where data originated and how it was transformed or transferred.
example: A reviewer traces an aggregate back to the source records and transformation steps.

definition: Public-key cryptography standards specify interoperable formats, algorithms, and procedures for systems using paired public and private keys.
example: An engineer checks a signing service against the applicable signature standard.

definition: Pug is a template language and engine with indentation-based syntax for generating HTML.
example: A site renders a list of products from records using one Pug template.

definition: Punctuation uses conventional written marks to organize text and clarify its structure and meaning.
example: An editor uses commas to separate items in a list.

definition: PuPHPet was a configuration generator for provisioning Vagrant development environments with Puppet.
example: A developer used it to generate a repeatable local PHP development setup.

definition: Puppet automates system configuration by specifying the desired state of managed resources.
example: An administrator sets the same package and configuration across servers.

definition: Puppeteer is a JavaScript library for controlling web browsers programmatically.
example: A developer captures a screenshot after a test page loads.

definition: PuTTY is a terminal client for connections such as SSH and serial sessions.
example: An administrator opens an authorized SSH session for routine maintenance.

definition: PyMongo is the MongoDB driver for Python, providing access to collections and database operations.
example: A Python service uses it to read application records.

definition: PyTables is a Python package for managing and querying structured data in HDF5 files.
example: An analyst reads a subset of a large scientific dataset stored in HDF5.

definition: Python for data analysis is using Python and its libraries to prepare, examine, and interpret data.
example: An analyst groups sales records by month and checks for missing values.

definition: Python Server Pages are a server-side templating approach that embeds Python logic in pages rendered into HTML.
example: A historical web application inserts a record into a generated HTML page.
sense_note: Multiple implementations share this label. This definition describes the general technique.

definition: Python Tools for Visual Studio provides Python editing, debugging, and project support within Microsoft Visual Studio.
example: A developer inspects variable values while stepping through a Python program.

definition: PyTorch is a tensor-computing library with automatic differentiation for building and training machine-learning models.
example: A developer computes gradients for a model during training.

definition: QARun was a Compuware tool for automating functional tests of application interfaces.
example: A tester replayed a recorded sequence to check a desktop application.
sense_note: Historical product. Verify branding and supported platforms from vendor archival material.

definition: Qlik Sense is an analytics platform for exploring data and building interactive visualizations and dashboards.
example: A team connects an operations dataset to a dashboard with filters.

definition: QlikView is a business intelligence product for building and using interactive data analysis applications.
example: A manager filters a sales analysis document by region.

definition: QS/1 is a name associated with software used to manage pharmacy operations.
example: A pharmacy uses management software to track prescriptions and dispensing workflows.
sense_note: Verify whether the intended sense is the company, the brand, or a specific product line.

definition: Qualitative data analysis interprets nonnumeric evidence to identify themes, patterns, and meanings.
example: A researcher codes interview transcripts and compares recurring themes.

definition: A queue management system coordinates how waiting items or people are ordered, routed, and served.
example: A clinic routes waiting patients to available service counters.
sense_note: Examples use service queues, while the general label may also occur in computing.

definition: QuickTime VR was an Apple technology for viewing interactive panoramas or rotatable objects.
example: A museum visitor could pan around a digitized exhibit space.

definition: Qumu is an enterprise video platform for publishing, streaming, and managing organizational video.
example: A company distributes a recorded training session to staff.
sense_note: Verify whether the label is intended to refer to the platform or the company.

definition: QuoteWerks is a quoting and proposal tool for assembling sales offers with products, prices, and terms.
example: A salesperson prepares and revises an itemized customer quote.

definition: Rack elevation drawings depict the physical position and height of equipment in a rack.
example: An installer checks which rack units are reserved for a network switch.

definition: radare2 is an open-source framework for inspecting and analyzing compiled programs.
example: A developer inspects their own compiled program to understand its binary layout.

definition: Rally Software is an agile delivery management platform for planning and tracking work across teams.
example: A product team tracks stories and dependencies across iterations.

definition: Rancher is a management platform for operating and administering Kubernetes clusters.
example: An operations team views multiple clusters through one management interface.

definition: A random forest combines many randomized decision trees to make a prediction by aggregating their outputs.
example: A classifier combines votes from trees trained with different samples or feature subsets.

definition: Random testing evaluates a system using test inputs sampled from a specified domain or distribution.
example: A tester generates varied valid input sizes for a library.

definition: Randomization uses chance to assign treatments, choose observations, or vary order according to a stated procedure.
example: A study randomly assigns participants to two conditions.

definition: RavenDB is a document database for storing and querying structured data as documents.
example: An application stores each customer profile as a document.

definition: Ray tracing calculates light transport or visibility by following rays and evaluating their intersections with scene geometry.
example: A renderer traces a ray to determine what surface is visible at a pixel.

definition: React is a JavaScript library for constructing user interfaces from components whose output can change with data.
example: A developer builds a list component that updates as filters change.

definition: ReactiveX is a family of libraries and interfaces for composing and transforming asynchronous streams through observable sequences.
example: An application filters and combines streams of interface events.

definition: Reading gauges is interpreting indicated measurements on an instrument scale or display.
example: A technician reads a pressure indicator in the units marked on the dial.

definition: Reading technical drawings is interpreting dimensions, views, symbols, and specifications in technical documentation.
example: A craftsperson identifies a hole diameter and its tolerance from a drawing.

definition: Reading to children is presenting a written text aloud in ways that help young listeners follow and engage with it.
example: An educator pauses after a picture-book page to ask what happened.

definition: ReadyAPI is a software suite for testing and validating application programming interfaces.
example: A quality engineer checks that a test API returns the expected response fields.

definition: Real estate market analysis uses property, transaction, supply, and demand information to evaluate market conditions.
example: An analyst compares recent sales of similar properties in the same area.

definition: Recruitment consulting advises organizations on finding, assessing, and hiring people for defined roles.
example: A consultant helps a team clarify requirements and structure candidate evaluation.
